newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone troops seize diamond mines in Koidu.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone troops seize diamond mines in Koidu.

text.p: Sierra Leonean soldiers have seized foreign-owned diamond mines in the eastern town of Koidu following Sunday's army coup, police and community leaders in the town said on Thursday.

The sources, contacted by telephone from Freetown, said the heavily-armed soldiers drove from Freetown in commandeered vehicles and opened fire to scare away owners of the mines and other businesses in the town.
Canadian, British and Belgian mine operators are among hundreds of foreigners who have taken refuge at beachside hotels in Freetown hoping to join evacuation flights.

"We want to come back and take over our businesses, but certainly not under the present instability. We will come back when democracy is restored in Sierra Leone," said one mine operator, who declined to be named.
Low-ranking soldiers ousted civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah on Sunday.

Diamonds are Sierra Leone's main export and foreign investors had hoped that the election of a civilian government in March 1996, and a peace accord signed with rebels of the Revolutionary United Front last November would improve the security situation.

In Massingbi, 50 km from Koidu, soldiers on Wednesday shot dead at least 20 members of a civilian militia loyal to Kabbah who had been stationed in the town before the coup to protect against rebel attacks, police in the regional capital Makeni said.

One of the first acts of the new Armed Forces Revolutionary Council was to ban the Kamajors, on whom Kabbah had come to rely against the rebels. They have refused to disband and have clashed with soldiers in several towns.
Community leaders in the area said Kamajors were gathering in Massingbi vowing revenge for Wednesday's killings. They feared an escalation of the violence.
